title: Set-Builder Notation and the Math Behind Comprehensions
explainer: Python's `[expr for x in seq if cond]` syntax is a direct descendant of mathematical set-builder notation ({x : P(x)}), filtered down through the languages SETL and Haskell, which Python's own developers have cited as comprehensions' ancestors on the python-dev mailing list. Reading `{len(w) for w in words}` as 'the set of len(w) such that w is in words' is exactly how a mathematician reads the braces version — and it explains why the expression comes first and the filtering condition comes last, the reverse of a procedural loop's order.
